cards.title: Distinction Between Uncertainty and Variability in Translation
cards.claim: In translational PK/PD modeling, 'uncertainty' refers to limited knowledge of the system (e.g., scaling error) and decreases as information accumulates, whereas 'variability' is an inherent property of the system (e.g., inter-individual differences) that does not decrease with larger sample sizes. Conflating these leads to misinterpretation of prediction intervals.
conditions: Applicable when defining input distributions for Monte Carlo simulations.
Requires explicit labeling of whether a distribution represents scaling uncertainty or population variability.
required_inputs: Literature or empirical data on the accuracy of scaling methods (to define uncertainty ranges).
Knowledge of population variability if distinct from scaling uncertainty.
limitations: The source notes that literature on correlations between PK/PD parameter uncertainties is scarce.
PD uncertainty is highly project-specific and harder to generalize than PK uncertainty.
cards.downstream_use: Guides the construction of input distributions for prospective human simulations, ensuring that confidence intervals reflect knowledge gaps rather than assumed biological spread.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
